The Director II, Transformation & Enablement will lead the development and execution of strategic initiatives designed to strengthen organizational effectiveness, accelerate capability building, and enable future growth across U.S. Market Access. This role will serve as the leader of a centralized Transformation & Enablement organization responsible for driving operational excellence, organizational effectiveness, strategic planning support, capability development, and enterprise transformation efforts across the Market Access organization.
The role will oversee a centralized Transformation & Enablement team responsible for Payer Strategy Enablement, Account Enablement, Future Fit capability development, and strategic transformation initiatives. This team will be accountable for developing and scaling the capabilities, tools, processes, governance, and ways of working that define the future operating model of U.S. Market Access. The Director II will serve as the orchestrator of Market Access transformation, partnering with senior leaders across the organization to identify emerging needs, align on future-state priorities, and drive implementation of capabilities that improve enterprise performance, agility, and competitiveness.
The position will partner closely with the Market Access Leadership Team to align priorities, drive strategic initiatives, improve organizational effectiveness, and ensure the organization has the capabilities, infrastructure, and support model necessary to execute in an increasingly complex and rapidly evolving access environment.
This role offers a unique opportunity to shape the future operating model of U.S. Market Access while influencing strategy, execution, talent development, innovation, and organizational transformation across one of AbbVie's most critical commercial capabilities.

Define and lead the long-term Transformation & Enablement vision for U.S. Market Access

title: Director, CMC Product Development - Late Stage, Operations
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube .
Purpose
The Product Development Director (PDD) will be a member of the Operations Strategy & Pipeline Leadership (OSPL) team within the Product Development, Science & Technology (PDS&T) organization. Reporting to one of the Therapeutic Area Leads, the PDD will be responsible for pipeline programs from a Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls (CMC) perspective. They will lead the Product Presentation and Device Strategy Team (PPDST) and build the CMC development strategy for the late-stage assets, aligning with the clinical and regulatory development strategy from the Asset Strategy Team (AST). The programs can span modalities and presentations. Modalities can include small molecules, biologics (protein, gene therapy, toxin etc.) and antibody drug conjugates.  Product presentations can include oral dose, parenteral and devices (therapeutics and aesthetic).
The PDD is accountable for creating a CMC development plan in collaboration with line functions and ensures strategic alignment with the enterprise functions (Clinical, Regulatory and Commercial) cross-functionally at the AST. The PDD is the spokesperson for CMC-related aspects at asset-level governances and represents the assets within Operations to ensure support of late-stage development activities and readiness for launch. They are responsible for communicating development and regulatory risks and seeking feedback from CMC leadership.
Responsibilities
Represents all CMC areas on the AST serving as spokesperson for the CMC project team and ensures information flow among the AST and all line functions. Ensures high quality science, technology, deliverables, and collaborates to ensure compliance with global regulatory and quality requirements. Participates in interactions with Regulatory and Health Authorities.
Critically evaluates and integrates drug substance, drug product, and device inputs to CMC team strategies and plans that align with corporate business objectives. description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
AbbVie Biologics Analytical Research & Development (Biologics Analytical R&D) is a global analytical sciences organization responsible for all CMC analytical activities related to the development of AbbVie's pharmaceutical products.  Our scope includes AbbVie's diverse pipeline of innovative therapeutic biologic medicines and spans from the selection of Discovery candidate molecules through the transition of analytical methods and testing to commercial labs to support product launch.  We are building a world-class team of scientists and leaders who will drive the advancement of industry-leading analytical capabilities and make meaningful contributions to advance AbbVie's pipeline of innovative medicines.  Careers in AbbVie Biologics Analytical R&D provide unique opportunities to work with global and cross-functional teams to drive exceptional science and innovative product development strategies.
The biologics characterization group develops state-of-the-art analytical techniques for in-depth characterization of therapeutic proteins and other novel biologic molecules using advanced, combined analytical techniques. We are looking for diverse candidates with strong scientific and leadership experience to join the AbbVie Analytical R&D team and can offer exciting and rewarding career opportunities for these candidates.
Responsibilities:
Act as a subject matter expert in BioARD, lead phase-appropriate analytical development strategies for biologics characterization including ADC, PDC, AOC, fusion proteins, multi-specific antibodies, and other novel modalities.
Design and execute the buildout of biotherapeutics extended characterization methods, to facilitate in-process analytics, batch release/stability, RS qualification, and comparability study.
Make lab-based, data-driven, and phase-appropriate contributions to project team and deliver results in a team-oriented setting and will work across scientific disciplines to drive programs through critical milestones.
Represent key area function in cross-functional project teams, provide hands-on analytical support, technical oversight to portfolios.
Collaborate and integrate scientific objectives associated with development of new/improved products or technology; contribute to scientific exchange and publications.
Author, review lab notebook, analytical report, and analytical sections of regulatory filings. Primary author of external publications, presentations, and patents. Present at leading scientific conferences.
May mentor/supervise a team of one or more, guide and evaluate the performance of those individuals; is accountable for the effective performance of the team/individuals.
BS or equivalent education with 14+ years of experience; MS or equivalent education with 12+ years of experience; PhD in scientific discipline (e.g., Analytical Chemistry, Biochemistry, or Biology) with typically 6+ years of industry experience, is required.
Demonstrated proficiency and substantial hands-on experience in mass spectrometry-based characterization of biologics, including intact/subunit analysis, peptide mapping, disulfide bond mapping, etc., as well as hands-on experience in mass spec data processing and interpretation using various MS software platforms.

Partner with communicators, business leaders, and subject-matter experts to turn complex topics into clear, compelling stories.
Support communications for functions across Adobe and gain exposure to different parts of the business.
Help plan and execute communications projects and campaigns from idea through launch.
Publish content across Adobe’s intranet and app, in-office digital signage, Slack, and other employee channels.
Design engaging, on-brand content using Adobe products.
Explore new, creative ways to communicate and connect with employees.

Currently enrolled full time and pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in English, Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, Marketing, or a related field; or equivalent degree required with an expected graduation date of December 2027–June 2028.

Outstanding abilities in writing, editing, and storytelling.
Strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

title: Program Manager , Amazon Leo
description:

Coexistence & RF Fundamentals: Strong grasp of RF transceiver architectures, in-device coexistence (IDC), antenna isolation, harmonics, intermodulation distortion (IMD), receiver desense, and multi-radio interference mitigation techniques.
Hands-on Validation Experience: Proven track record of system test, integration, or validation using commercial wireless network emulators (e.g., Keysight, Rohde & Schwarz, Anritsu) and RF instrumentation (spectrum analyzers, signal generators, power meters).
Automation & Scripting: Strong proficiency in Python for test automation, instrument control (SCPI/VISA), and automated parsing/analysis of large log datasets.

title: US Wearables Analytics & Individual AI Lead
description:

title: Product Compliance Engineer
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Base is hiring a Compliance Engineer to own the certification path for our batteries, inverters, grid-connected devices, and solar products. You'll take each product from early design through certification and launch, run our relationships with NRTLs and standards bodies, and make sure compliance never slows a product down.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own relationships with Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratories (NRTLs), test labs, and standards bodies.

 - Build compliance into product requirements early, so engineering designs to the standard from day one.

 - Interpret, and when needed challenge, how standards apply across battery, inverter, and solar products.

 - Plan and run certification programs: test plans, setup, execution, and data analysis.

 - Review and approve hardware and system designs for compliance.

 - Work with firmware and controls engineers so software behavior supports certification.

 - Track new and changing standards, flag roadmap impact, and represent Base in working groups.

 - Be the internal expert on NEC and UL requirements.

 - Document processes, findings, and gaps so we stay audit-ready.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.

 - Experience taking a grid-tied product from concept through full certification.

 - Deep working knowledge of UL 1741, UL 9540, UL 9540A, UL 1973, and IEEE 1547.

 - Strong grasp of the NEC as it applies to energy storage and distributed energy resources.

 - Ability to turn standards language into clear engineering requirements.

 - Confidence pushing back on overly conservative interpretations of a standard.




PREFERRED SKILLS

 - Solar and PV standards: UL 3741, UL 2703, UL 61730, and UL 1703.

 - FCC Part 15 Subpart B EMI testing for power electronics.

 - UL 9540A thermal runaway fire testing.

 - Participation in standards committees or working groups.




ABOUT THE TEAM

Our compliance team makes sure certification is never the reason a Base product ships late. We build standards into requirements from day one, run every certification program with test labs, and help shape the standards that govern home energy storage. Homeowners across the country rely on Base for whole-home backup and lower electricity bills. Our network of home batteries also helps keep the grid stable as demand climbs from AI, electrification, and extreme weather. We build in-house and expand at a speed and cost incumbents can't match, and this team makes that possible.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

About the Role
At DoorDash we are redefining what it means to be a designer. We are building toward a team of makers, builders, and doers. Between 2005 and 2015, "web designer" became "product designer" and the scope widened. The same shift is happening now, as LLMs expand that scope again, toward strategy on one end and direct execution on the other. As a Staff Visual Designer, you'll practice this build-first way of working with real autonomy: using AI-native tools and code to move from idea to shipped work quickly, and owning craft decisions end to end rather than checking each one against a brief.
You'll join Studio Central, a net-new Product Design team sitting at the intersection of product, brand, and innovation. Studio Central is a global team within Studio, DoorDash's Product Design organization, supporting DoorDash, Wolt, Deliveroo, and 7Rooms. We own how brand shows up in the product experience, partnering closely with Marketing and Product teams to shape cohesive, high-quality work and to help define the foundations, vision, and future state of design across our portfolio. Our work spans major brand moments, merchandising, and the systems that connect it all.
Studio Central's systems and standards are still being built, and everyone building here, regardless of level, has real input into what they become. You'll have full ownership over your own craft and projects, and a real voice in the standards, rituals, and craft bar the whole team ends up working from, not reacting to a framework someone else already finished, but helping shape it as it forms.
We operate in a hybrid working model, 1-2 days out of one of our Design Hubs, the rest working from home.
Your primary impact is craft and output: shipping high-quality, on-brand work across the campaigns, seasonal moments, and merchandising pushes Studio Central owns, with less oversight than earlier-career roles and more responsibility for getting it right yourself. Your secondary impact is revenue, in the same way: the work you ship well, and the craft feedback you give to the designers around you, is part of what raises the expression bar across DoorDash, Wolt, Deliveroo, and 7Rooms as a whole.
You're excited about this opportunity because you will...
Own end-to-end visual craft on brand moments, campaigns, and merchandising pushes, from concept through shipped, production-ready work, with less oversight than earlier-career roles
Mentor other designers as needed, sharing craft feedback and helping them build range, without formal authority over their work
Help build and pressure-test the design systems, component libraries, and AI-powered tooling as a team, whether that's proposing the first version or stress-testing someone else's, and speak up early rather than reacting to a finished one
Practice influencing without authority: bring a strong point of view into rooms with Product, Marketing, and creative stakeholders, and back it up with working prototypes rather than title
Build real range across the full workflow, from rough concept to production-ready execution, and hand off cleanly to engineering so nothing gets lost in translation
We're excited about you because you have...
A portfolio that shows strong, considered visual craft, systems thinking, or brand work at a senior level, even if you haven't yet led an org-wide initiative
Comfort moving between art-direction tools like Figma and Illustrator and shipping in code, or you're closing that gap quickly
A habit of treating a new tool or technique as an experiment worth running, not a decision you need to get right the first time, you'll ship a handful of rough attempts in something you picked up last week before you'd sit through a training on it
Experience giving craft feedback to other designers, even informally, and helping them get sharper
A track record of shipping ambiguous briefs to a high bar without heavy oversight

This is an individual contributor role with responsibility for leading technical revenue accounting assessments for assigned business lines, products, and transactions. You will partner with Business Development, Product, Sales, Legal, Finance, and operational accounting teams to evaluate proposed contract terms and product offerings, explain their accounting and financial statement implications, and help stakeholders assess alternatives.
You will apply US GAAP, particularly ASC 606, to complex transactions; document clear, well-supported accounting conclusions; and translate those conclusions into practical implementation requirements. Document accounting conclusions. Prepare technical accounting memos and position papers that clearly explain relevant facts, applicable guidance, significant judgments, and conclusions.

Support operational implementation. Translate accounting conclusions into requirements for billing, revenue recognition, financial reporting, and controls, partnering with operational accounting teams to support accurate execution.
Strengthen policies, processes, and controls. Develop and maintain revenue accounting policies, guidance, and training materials, and identify opportunities to improve contract review processes and related controls.
Support audits and financial reporting. Work with accounting leadership and external auditors to address technical accounting questions, explain significant judgments, and support quarterly and annual reporting as needed.

title: Electrical Engineer II, Advanced Product Development
description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form! 



In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

Form's Advanced Product Development team is responsible for architecting and designing the next generation of our iron-air battery system — the cell, module, pack, and the support systems that keep them running reliably for decades in the field. We work ahead of our production programs, translating breakthrough electrochemistry and system requirements into electrical, controls, and test systems that can scale to high-volume manufacturing.

We're hiring an Electrical Engineer II to design, build, troubleshoot, and test the control systems and test assets that support development of our next generation of iron-air batteries. As part of our Advanced Product Development team in Somerville, MA, you will spend much of your time in the lab: wiring and commissioning control systems, bringing up new hardware, diagnosing electrical and controls faults, and running system-level tests. You will work with guidance from senior electrical engineers and alongside mechanical and systems engineers and technicians to turn test requirements into safe, reliable, well-documented hardware. This is an exciting opportunity to deliver our sustainable multi-day energy storage solution to the grid!

Relocation assistance is available. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Design, build, wire, and check out control systems for test assets, working from schematics and BOMs through fabrication and documentation.

 - Troubleshoot electrical and controls issues on test assets and prototype hardware, finding root causes with scopes, meters, and data logs and implementing fixes.

 - Bring up and commission new test assets in the lab, including point-to-point checkout, sensor and instrument verification, and functional testing of safety interlocks.

 - Plan and run system-level tests: write test procedures, collect and review data, and report results and issues to the team.

 - Program and modify PLC and HMI logic for test assets with guidance from senior engineers, and keep eCAD schematics, BOMs, and cable/harness documentation current.

 - Partner with mechanical, systems, and test engineers and technicians on tight timelines, and champion lab and electrical safety when introducing new processes, prototype hardware, or test methods.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - Degree in Electrical Engineering or related field; Bachelor's with 1+ years experience in control panel design, PLC programming, or test/automation equipment, or Master's with research or professional engineering experience.

 - Experience with PLC programming (e.g., Beckhoff TwinCAT, Allen-Bradley, or similar) and HMI development, including debugging logic on live hardware.

 - Ability to read and work from electrical schematics; experience with an eCAD package (AutoCAD Electrical, ePLAN, or SolidWorks Electrical) is a plus.

 - Hands-on lab skills: panel wiring, troubleshooting with scopes and meters, commissioning hardware, and planning and running system-level tests.

 - Familiarity with NFPA 70/79 and UL 508A practices for industrial control panels.

 - Exposure to sensors, data acquisition, power distribution, and industrial communication protocols (e.g., EtherCAT, Modbus, CAN).

 - Experience in energy storage, batteries, or another safety-critical hardware industry is a plus.

 #LI-Onsite



Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here.

ROLE DESCRIPTION

Form Energy is hiring a Electronics Test Engineer II for the AMU (Auxiliary Management Unit) to join our BMS Test team. In this role, you will be responsible for executing design verification and validation testing at the component, board, and system level for our AMU hardware. 

 

Physically, the AMU PCBA sits inside the AMU Panel assembly along with the HIgh Voltage DC Shunt board which is responsible for measuring efficiency of our system, UPS, and PSUs. It acts as a critical zone controller responsible for communication, network security, high-voltage/high-current sensing, power distribution, actuation, safety/fault management, and UPS management.

 

You will ensure that AMU electronics meet stringent functional, reliability, safety, and compliance requirements through structured test campaigns. You’ll collaborate closely with hardware, firmware, and systems engineers to validate designs that are central to the safe and reliable operation of our multi-megawatt battery systems.This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the scaling of our battery technology and be part of the growth of a fast-moving company with breakthrough technology and an incredible mission!

 

Relocation assistance is available. 

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Test Strategy & DVP: Be part of the Development for comprehensive test plans, DVP&Rs, and verification protocols for the AMU PCBA and its integrated panel assembly components.

 - Communication Protocol Verification: Validate safety-critical and non-safety communication interfaces including CAN-FD (to ZMUs), Ethernet (to ZMUs and upstream QMU), and dedicated RS485 (for UPS management).

 - Sensing Subsystem Validation: Execute test setups to verify precision sensing capabilities: Pack HV voltage (-1 to 1600V via HVDC Shunt resistor divider), Pack HV current (-500A to 500A via shunt R4), 48V PSU/UPS monitoring (0-60V), 48V total current draw (0-40A), and auxiliary temperatures.

 - Actuation & Power Distribution: Verify HV contactor control (pack connect/disconnect), heater SSR control, and power routing from dual 48V PSUs and the 48V UPS down to the ZMUs.

 - Safety & Fault Management: Rigorously test Hardware Over-Current Protection, fault loop logic, and Functional Safety (FuSa) testing.

 - Data Analysis & Root-Cause: Analyze test data, generate detailed reports, and collaborate with design engineers to root-cause board or firmware anomalies found during testing.

 - Test Automation: Contribute to test automation frameworks (utilizing Pytest) to optimize repeatability and scale verification throughput.

 


WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or related field.

 - 1+ years of experience in PCBA hardware testing. Must have robust board-level and system-level validation experience.

 - Some experience in firmware verification, utilizing Pytest or similar unit testing frameworks. Comfort with debugging tools, Linux environments, and Test-Driven Development (TDD)

 - Hands-on experience with test instrumentation (oscilloscopes, power supplies, data acquisition systems, environmental chambers).

 - Hands-on experience with high-voltage/high-current test instrumentation (power supplies, electronic loads)

 - Demonstrated ability to work with test plans, execute verification activities, and communicate findings effectively.

 - Domain Knowledge: Understanding of communication protocols (CAN-FD, Ethernet, RS485), power distribution topologies, and functional safety frameworks.

description:
Job Description:
Human Resources Specialist
ABOUT ITW MEDICAL:
ITW (NYSE: ITW) is a Fortune 300 global multi-industrial manufacturing leader with revenue of $16 billion in 2025. ITW’s approximately 43,000 dedicated colleagues around the world thrive in the company’s decentralized and entrepreneurial culture.
ITW Medical, a division of ITW, is comprised of two highly respected brands- Coeur and Filtertek, supplying critical filtration and flow control solutions to global OEM’s, serving Surgical, Infusion, Bioprocessing and Diagnostic Imaging end markets.
Position Summary:
The Human Resources Specialist supports organizational effectiveness by collecting, analyzing, and interpreting human resources data to drive informed business decisions. This role partners with the HR Director and leaders to support workforce planning, recruitment, onboarding, employee retention, compliance, compensation, training, and performance management initiatives. The HR Analyst develops actionable insights, maintains key HR metrics and dashboards, and makes recommendations that enhance talent acquisition, employee engagement, and overall organizational performance.
Duties and Responsibilities:
Analyze workforce trends and organizational metrics to identify talent gaps, skill gaps, succession planning opportunities, retention risks, and workforce needs. Provide data-driven recommendations that support organizational growth, workforce forecasting, and strategic business objectives.
Support talent management initiatives, including performance management, talent reviews, succession planning, career development, and competency framework administration. Assist with goal setting, performance evaluations, calibration activities, reporting, and the maintenance of career paths and development tools.
Lead the administration and continuous improvement of employee recognition programs by evaluating participation and effectiveness, maintaining existing initiatives, and recommending new programs that enhance employee engagement, retention, and organizational culture.
Conduct compensation analyses, including salary benchmarking, job classification reviews, pay equity assessments, and market comparisons. Present findings and recommendations to HR leadership.
Support recruitment and onboarding efforts, including full-cycle recruiting activities, onboarding program administration, employer branding initiatives, talent pipeline development, and analysis of recruiting and onboarding effectiveness metrics.
Develop and maintain relationships with external recruiting partners, educational institutions, and community organizations to support workforce needs and build diverse talent pipelines.
Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local employment laws and regulations, including data privacy, record retention, employee records management, compensation practices, and other regulatory requirements.
Conduct periodic audits of HR processes and records, including employee data, compensation, job classifications, and compliance requirements, and recommend corrective actions or process improvements as needed.
Evaluate, develop, and recommend improvements to HR policies, programs, and processes in partnership with HR leadership and site HR teams, supporting implementation and communication efforts.
Collect, validate, analyze, and maintain HR data from multiple sources including HRIS, payroll systems, surveys, exit interviews, performance evaluations, applicant tracking systems, and other workforce management tools.
Develop and maintain HR dashboards, reports, and key performance indicators (KPIs) related to headcount, turnover, retention, compensation, recruiting, onboarding, employee engagement, performance management, and workforce planning.
Perform other related duties as assigned.

Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills.
Excellent verbal, written, and presentation communication skills.
Strong attention to detail with the ability to manage multiple priorities.

Thorough understanding of federal, state, and local employment laws and regulations.

Experience working with HRIS, payroll systems, applicant tracking systems (ATS), and workforce analytics platforms.
Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion.

Ability to occasionally lift and carry up to 15 pounds.

title: Lead Director of Photography
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function
The Lead Director of Photography is a creative and craft leader within Intuitive’s Studio, responsible for advancing the visual language of moving image, motion, and photography across Brand & Creative.
This is a hands-on role for someone with strong visual instincts, a clear point of view, and the range to move between creative development and execution. They can define how something should look and feel, then step behind the camera and make it happen.
The Lead DP partners closely with designers, art directors, writers, producers, editors, motion designers, and, as needed, strategy and social teams. They contribute as a creative peer to senior creative talent and executive creative leadership, confidently advocating for ideas while remaining curious, adaptable, and open to feedback from anyone.
Moving image is central to the role. The Lead DP also leads the development of Studio’s photography practice, creating high-end photography on select projects and elevating standards, practices, and output across the team. This responsibility does not include direct management of photographers.
We’re looking for someone who loves making things, brings fresh thinking, shares knowledge generously, and is as willing to do the heavy lifting as they are to lead the room.
What You’ll Do
Define and evolve our visual language
Advance Studio’s approach to moving image, motion, and photography in close partnership with Creative.
Contribute from the earliest stages of development, translating ideas, stories, and brand objectives into distinct visual approaches.
Bring production craft into the development of ideas, helping shape what we make and how we make it.
Explore new approaches to shooting, editing, lighting, composition, and motion that strengthen storytelling and help evolve the brand’s look and feel.
Lead cinematography and filmmaking
Serve as lead DP across Studio productions, owning the approach to camera, lighting, lenses, composition, movement, coverage, and image capture.
Develop treatments, visual references, shot lists, and storyboards, including rough sketches when useful.
Direct projects, talent, interviews, or scenes when the assignment calls for it.
Lead camera and lighting crews with clear direction, thoughtful preparation, and sound creative and technical judgment.
Adapt to changing conditions while protecting the story, creative intent, and quality of the work.
Elevate the photography practice
Shoot high-end photography on select assignments that benefit from your expertise.
Establish and continually raise standards for lighting, composition, technique, and execution across photography produced by Studio and its partners.
Improve photography workflows, equipment practices, and quality standards.
Guide and mentor teammates and external partners through constructive feedback and shared expertise.
Shape the story through post
Partner with editors and motion designers to develop new approaches to structure, pacing, rhythm, movement, and sound.
Bring ideas and constructive creative challenge that help teammates expand how they tell stories.
Contribute hands-on editing support when needed.
On larger projects, contribute to casting, music, editorial, color, and finishing, staying engaged through final delivery.
Work independently and collaboratively
Independently plan and execute smaller shoots, including assignments without a dedicated producer.
Collaborate effectively within larger teams of creatives, producers, directors, agencies, production partners, and specialized crews.
Recommend an approach and production scale appropriate to the idea, budget, schedule, and intended result.
Prepare thoroughly, solve problems resourcefully, and follow through on commitments.
Strengthen the team
Lead through the quality of your work, the clarity of your ideas, and how you treat people.
Share knowledge and mentor teammates through the work, helping develop their craft, judgment, and confidence.
Give useful feedback, welcome different perspectives, and share credit.
Contribute beyond your own assignments to improve the work and capabilities of Studio and Brand & Creative.
What You Bring
A strong body of work demonstrating accomplished cinematography, high-quality photography, and thoughtful visual storytelling. Please identify your contribution to each project.
Deep practical knowledge of cameras, lenses, lighting, composition, movement, exposure, and image capture.
The ability to connect visual decisions to a story, audience, and creative idea.
The confidence and judgment to present ideas, lead a shoot, and collaborate as a peer with senior creative partners.
The ability to communicate visually through references, treatments, shot lists, storyboards, or sketches.
Working editing proficiency and an understanding of editorial, motion, music, color, and finishing.
Resourcefulness across small independent assignments and larger productions.
Curiosity, initiative, reliability, and a commitment to developing both your own work and the people around you.
How You Work Matters
Low ego is essential. You bring conviction without defensiveness, take feedback seriously regardless of its source, and treat everyone with respect. You remain willing to execute the details and do the heavy lifting, regardless of experience or seniority.
We welcome both emerging creative leaders ready for broader responsibility and experienced practitioners eager to contribute and mentor. Your work, judgment, and approach to collaboration matter.
Travel: Approximately 20% travel is expected, depending on production needs.
Required Skills, Experience, and Training
12+ years of experience
Experience working in or closely with Brand & Creative teams.
A bachelor's degree in film, design, media arts, communications, or adjacent fields; equivalent professional experience is also acceptable.

Our team designs and builds the embedded platform software infrastructure that supports critical
performance, safety and user-facing features of the da Vinci™ Surgical System, Intuitive’s flagship product.
We’re looking for a high energy, experienced embedded software engineer to take technical ownership
across our embedded platform software stack.
In this role, you will lead board bring-up initiatives, drive architectural decision for our next-generation platforms, and serve as a technical anchor for the team – mentoring junior engineers and collaborating cross-functionally with hardware, system software, and FPGA teams. Partner with and technically guide hardware engineers to identify, root-cause and resolve board-level issues during early development phases – serving as the primary software interface for cross-functional hardware bring-up

Mentor junior and mid-level engineers through code reviews, technical guidance, and hands-on debugging support – actively contributing to the growth of the team.
Author and maintain technical documentation including design specifications, bring-up procedures, and failure analysis reports in compliance with FDA-regulated development processes.

Minimum of 8 years of related experience and a Bachelor's degree; or 6 years experience and a Master's degree; or a PhD with 3 years of experience; or equivalent experience
Expert-level proficiency in C or C++ for embedded systems development, including memory management, real-time constraints, and performance-critical code
Experience in bare-metal, embedded Linux, including kernel internals, custom device driver development, BSP bring-up, and user space application development
Proficiency with embedded development and debugging tools including GDB, JTAG, logic analyzers, oscilloscopes, and cross-compilation toolchains

Debugging and root-cause analysis skills, with a track record of resolving complex, multi-layer Hardware-FPGA-software integration failures in time-critical environments
Demonstrated ability to mentor and technically develop junior and mid-level engineers
Effective written and verbal communication skills for technical documentation and cross-functional team collaboration

Hands-on experience with NVIDIA Jetson platforms (TX2/Xavier/Orin or similar) or comparable ARM-based SOCs in a production embedded environment
Hands-on experience with GPU acceleration (CUDA) and hardware-accelerated inference frameworks (TensorRT) in production embedded systems
Experience with QNX RTOS or other real-time operating systems in safety-critical applications.
Proficiency in Python and bash scripting for test automation, bootup design, and build system integration
Demonstrated ability to root cause complex hardware-software interactions
Demonstrated experience in and comfort with all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, implementation, debug, verification, validation, and transfer to manufacturing
Experience designing software products in an FDA or other regulated industry or for mission critical applications; comfortable with concepts of design input, design output, traceability, risk analysis, and mitigations

Primary Function of Position
The DaVinci Specialist (DVS) will provide expert clinical & technical support, build, customize and coordinate education & training to physicians, nurses, and hospital staff on the use of DaVinci surgery, devices and therapies. This role partners closely with the sales team, specifically the Clinical Sales Representative and Clinical Sales Manager, to ensure safe and effective product adoption and quality control while driving positive patient outcomes.
The DaVinci Specialist is a dedicated program execution & clinical education partner for hospitals running a da Vinci robotic surgery program.   Based on its expertise, this role focuses on identifies and tailors the nature and extent of staff in-servicing, day-to-day program execution, technology onboarding and operational support, communicating identified needs to hospital OR operations and leadership. The DVS will work alongside the daVinci Clinical Sales Representative .
Essential Job Duties
Collaboration & Field Partnership (Within a CSM Team)
Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.
Lead account support plans that drive safe program execution and increase customer autonomy over time, including setting objectives, timelines and resources for relevant customers, in consultation with CSR/CSM.
Identify, solicit and provide field feedback and customer insights to internal teams to improve training, support resources, and customer experience.
Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.
Clinical & Technical Support
Identify and provide on-site, non-scrubbed operating room support for procedures utilizing the da Vinci Surgical System and associated technologies.
Support OR teams with room readiness and procedural workflow, including system setup support, docking workflow support, and intraoperative troubleshooting.
Serve as a clinical product expert to help ensure optimal, safe system use and adherence to applicable IFUs, hospital policies, and safety protocols.

Datacenter Operations
Encourages the sharing of expertise in and provides guidance on standard processes and procedures for preparing, installing, performing diagnostics, troubleshooting, replacing, and decommissioning IT datacenter technology(ies) and equipment. Encourages the sharing of expertise and provides guidance on the functions of, and interactions between cabling infrastructure, network, server, and storage equipment. Develops awareness of Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL) Foundation components: Incident Management and Change Management.   Provides guidance on, and holds a team of technicians accountable for compliance with Data Center business unit policies, procedures, and deadlines. Proactively reviews and provides feedback regarding Data Center business unit policies, procedures, and deadlines. Resolves issues related to compliance or operational assurance activities directly, or with assistance from compliance colleagues and/or business partners. Provides input on improvement plan components for service delivery gaps or challenges.   Ensures a team of technicians can complete assigned tickets efficiently and in alignment with relevant Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) per task type. Supports escalation of challenging or complex tickets to internal business partners and appropriately summarizes relevant issues for communication to direct-line management. Coordinates and assigns tasks to technicians, and/or provides input or coordination with appropriate program managers and direct-line management for ticket assignment automation to provide direction as needed, to ensure work is appropriately allocated to meet Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) per task type. Monitors progress of tickets assigned to teams of technicians and adjusts where necessary, to meet established Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) per task type. Analyzes data related to technicians' performance on tickets and shares with direct-line management.   Advises on and reviews suggested modifications to process and procedures to manage changes and drive improvement in service quality and/or efficiency. Proactively investigates, evaluates, and analyzes changes. Reviews Process Change Notifications (PCNs) to evaluate impact on service execution and shares relevant information about change with stakeholders across functions and disciplines to mitigate the impact they may have on others. Encourages technicians to ask questions when they do not have required information, resolves others' questions in a timely manner, and may provide feedback on changes to processes to direct-line management, standards management teams, and/or project, program, or special initiative managers. May escort third party vendors or IT support on-premises at data centers or network sites. Participates in identifying the root cause of any physical security access violations and manages corrective actions and escalations related to technician violations of physical security procedures or policies. Maintains responsibility for client and technician team interactions for escalations and/or engagements between them and other internal business partners. Partners with internal and external stakeholders to manage the removal of risks to personnel and/or resource availability, performance, and compliance.   Identifies and assigns required training as applicable across all technician job focus areas and workloads (i.e., Break fix, Deployment, Simple Change, Decommission, IT Critical Environment) along with Personnel Management training in a timely manner per direct-line management assignment(s) and validates completion of assigned training by team members. Shares feedback from reviews with technicians to drive improvement in meeting KPI expectations and sharing learnings from reviews with direct-line management. People Management
Managers deliver success through empowerment and accountability by modeling, coaching, and caring. Model: Live our culture. Embody our values. Practice our leadership principles. Coach: Define team objectives and outcomes. Enable success across boundaries. Help the team adapt and learn. Care: Attract and retain great people. Follows procedures to immediately engage Designated Responsible Individuals (DRIs) for appropriate communication, reporting, and incident management of data center technical or safety related incidents with direct-line management, internal business partners, and impacted engineering group contacts. Participates in bridge calls to provide details on incident status and executes on-site follow-up actions as directed if necessary. May leverage learnings to contribute to the improvement of quality of service and support.   Coordinates training packages for technicians on procedures for installation, deployment, upgrade, refresh, simple change, decommission and/or replacement of infrastructure cabling, network, storage, or server equipment. Creates schedules for shift-based technicians to ensure positioning and availability to execute work as defined by organizational standards, negotiates with internal team colleagues to organize project timelines, with guidance from direct-line management, and appropriate notification to stakeholders.   Manages assigned projects or programs to meet service delivery objectives. Participates in pilot programs or task forces to ensure smooth implementation for future service delivery as directed.   Proactively reviews schedules and avoids conflicts when possible. Identifies, coordinates, manages expectations, and offers alternatives when defining technical solutions in light of ongoing operations and procedures (e.g., schedule, technical feasibility, policy, procedure, tools).   Evaluates procedures for performing quality checks to ensure they align with compliance standards and process adherence, and takes responsibility for impact to Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) by task type of work performed by technicians. Identifies errors in deployment standards or Network Design Templates (NDTs) and coordinates directly with internal business partners, technologists, or subject matter experts (SMEs) to develop corrections as needed.   Evaluates diagnostic and troubleshooting processes and suggests improvements. title: Logistics Technician
description:
Overview
As a Logistics Technician, you will perform cycle audits, execute incoming/outgoing deliveries, coordinate security escorts for third-party vendors, and document inbound and outbound deliveries. This opportunity will allow you to deepen your knowledge of inventory management principles, warranty process management, data bearing device destruction and advance your career in the process.
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I DIAT, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 Data Centers in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our data center design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties
Responsibilities
Customer Service
Maintains a strong focus to understand the impact of their work when completing tickets and assigned Inventory and Asset Management (IAM) tasks. Ensures IAM tasks are completed accurately as requested, as well as meet company and industry standards and policies. Becomes familiar with guidelines set by the Microsoft contractual agreements with suppliers and maintains a strong customer focus. Recognizes potential stakeholder impact of external and internal events and issues, communicates potential impact, and plans for impact accordingly.
Data Bearing Device (DBD) Destruction Performs destruction of data bearing devices (DBD) following all Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and Microsoft policies as necessary. Ensures DBD serial number matches with database. Supports decommissioning servers, maintaining compliance and meeting Service Level Agreements (SLAs).
Fleet Management Performs weekly vehicle inspections.
Inbound and Outbound Logistics
Performs data entry to document inbound and outbound packages. Executes incoming/outgoing deliveries as instructed by management (e.g. purchase order [PO] receiving, Rack Movement Supervisor [RMS] activities). Ensures accurate documentation of incoming and outgoing deliveries as well as records. Applies appropriate customs documentations and standards for outbound packages.
IT Inventory Management Develops working knowledge of stock control and inventory management practices and procedures. Performs cycle audits and data corrections to ensure all inventory controls are met and helps report and reconcile inventory discrepancies. Ensures detailed physical inventory tracking and staging, identifying opportunities to improve inventory and address space constraints. Performs material movement, including shipping/receiving and inventory management per standard process.
Operational Excellence Follows existing procedures to run processes and ensures execution with consistency, accuracy, and timeliness of delivery. Completes required security and data management training while complying with security and data management procedures/policies. Participates in training for relevant site-specific procedures and tools (e.g., forklift, pallet jacks, technician on-hand processes, inventory maintenance software, RMA portals, Rack Movement).
Procurement Notifies management about ordering stock shortages. Escalates any issues to management.
Safety Practices Complies with security and data management policies. Escalates any security or safety incidents. Coordinates with security escorts for third-party vendors. Engages in Task Hazard Analysis (THA) consistently for every task to be performed and ensures sign off from appropriate person for any related risks. Conducts rack movement activities, supporting training on devices and tools and upholding safety standards. Follows established protocols on dealing with unsafe materials out of containment, leveraging safety alert system, escalating to management, and properly disposing of them.
Tactical Shift Management Performs assigned tasks and escalates issues during high-volume work activity or escalation-based situations. Seeks guidance from management before proceeding with the next step of a process. Begins monitoring inbound and outbound schedules, escalating deviations from scheduling, with guidance.
Travel and Work Hours (Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles) May travel up to 25%, typically domestically to and from multiple locations during the workday. Working 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
Warranty Process Management Engages supplier to initiate warranty claim when automation is not available and processes the orders. Processes failed vendor hardware devices using online/other tools, including information processing, packaging, shipment, and receipt of return for Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) and non-RMA devices. Performs manual return processes for non-RMA failed parts. Begins to perform manual ordering processes of Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) parts. Follows all Service Level Agreements (SLAs) related to RMA and non-RMA warranty process.

description:
Overview
Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment.
The AI & Human Systems  group at Microsoft Research New York City (MSR NYC) and Microsoft Research New England (MSR NE) is seeking multiple Research Interns.
AI & Human Systems brings together researchers and applied scientists who have been part of the Fairness, Accountability, Transparency, and Ethics in AI  (FATE),  Sociotechnical Alignment Center  (STAC),  Economics and Computation , and  Computational Social Science  (CSS) groups. This posting is for candidates interested in working with researchers and applied scientists across any of these areas. Group members collaborate extensively with one another and with other groups across Microsoft.
The group shares a common goal: a world where AI boosts productivity, accelerates innovation, and helps people flourish by focusing their attention, enhancing their capabilities, and safeguarding their agency. Research Interns will contribute to this goal by working with mentors on research that advances it.
Our research draws on diverse disciplinary perspectives to study, measure, and design AI systems and understand their effects on people, teams, organizations, markets, economies, and societies. Topics include, but are not limited to: AI measurement and evaluation; measuring the impacts of AI on individuals, organizations, and society; human–AI interaction and meaningful human engagement with AI; and the design of agentic systems, markets, and institutions that shape how AI participates in the economy and society.
Applicants should demonstrate an interest in studying AI and human systems, a desire to work in a highly interdisciplinary environment, and experience using AI to thoughtfully enhance their own research. We welcome applicants pursuing a doctoral degree in technical fields (e.g., machine learning, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, statistics, computer science), economics, computational social science, or sociotechnical fields (e.g., human–computer interaction, information science, law, linguistics, science and technology studies) as well as JD candidates. title: Controls Engineer, Power Generation and Microgird
description:
About the Team

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital and delivery partners, is building the infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems. The Data Center Engineering team defines repeatable technical standards and carries them through design, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness. The team works across data center facilities, power generation, compute infrastructure, construction, procurement, and operations to deliver reliable capacity at unprecedented scale and speed.

About the Role

We are seeking a Controls Engineer to design, program, integrate and commission on-site power generation and microgrid control systems serving large AI data center campuses. You will own control architecture and functional requirements across generation packages, balance-of-plant systems, electrical protection, microgrid controls, and data center monitoring. You will work from concept through factory testing, site commissioning, performance validation, and operational improvement.

This role requires hands-on experience with industrial control systems, including PLC and DCS programming, plant-level control sequences, equipment integration, simulation, testing and commissioning. The engineers will work with equipment vendors, system integrators and the broader data center team to make sure the complete power system operates safely and reliably across normal and failure conditions.

Travel: 50%

Key Responsibilities

 - Power Generation and Microgrid Controls
   
   - Design, program and commission plant power controllers (PPCs) and microgrid control systems for gas turbine and reciprocating engine power plants.
   
   - Develop control sequences for grid-connected, islanded and transition modes, including startup, shutdown, synchronization, load sharing, import/export control, load shedding, black start, restoration and resynchronization.
   
   - Coordinate active power, reactive power, voltage and frequency controls across generators, energy storage, MV UPS and other distributed energy resources.
   
   - Define how the plant responds to generator trips, loss of utility power, large load changes, equipment failures and loss of communication.
   
   - Work with OEMs to define the boundaries between turbine or engine controls, generator controls, the PPC, protection systems and data center controls.

 - Electrical systems and utility interconnection
   
   - Review utility and transmission-provider interconnection requirements and translate them into plant control, protection, metering, communications and testing requirements.
   
   - Work with utility and equipment vendors to define controls and interfaces at the point of interconnection, including power limits, voltage and frequency response, reactive, power factor, telemetry and dispatch.
   
   - Review interconnection studies, operating procedures and test requirements, and track the actions needed to demonstrate compliance.
   
   - Work with Engineer-Of-Record (EOR) to review load-flow, short-circuit, stability, step-load and electromagnetic transient (EMT) studies. Use the results to develop control settings, sequences and test cases.

 - Control Architecture:
   
   - Develop and review functional design specifications (FDS), sequences of operation, network architecture diagrams, I/O lists and alarm philosophies.
   
   - Review P&IDs and instrumentation for generation-plant systems, including fuel gas, cooling, lubrication and other balance-of-plant equipment.
   
   - Define equipment interfaces, control modes, permissives, interlocks and failure responses between OEM packages and the plant control system.

 - Real-Time Simulation and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing:
   
   - Develop and execute real-time simulation and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) tests for generation and microgrid control systems using RTDS and RSCAD.
   
   - Work with internal engineering teams and equipment vendors to build and validate representative models of the electrical system, from the generation plant and utility interconnection through the data center distribution system to representative GPU rack loads.
   
   - Develop and execute test cases for normal operation, mode changes, load steps, trips, faults, and system failures.
   
   - Compare simulation and HIL results with equipment data, factory test results and field performance. Document model assumptions and limitations.

 - Testing, commissioning and delivery
   
   - Develop and review FAT, SAT and integrated systems test plans for plant and microgrid controls.
   
   - Participate in factory testing, site testing, energization support, tuning and commissioning of generation and data center power systems.
   
   - Troubleshoot controls and system-integration issues using controller data, alarms, event records, trends and test results.
   
   - Work with OEMs, EPCs, utilities and system integrators to resolve interface gaps and track issues through closure.
   
   - Coordinate the handover of final project deliverables, including software, configurations, backups, test records, operating instructions and training, to the data center operations team.

Qualifications

 - 8+ years of hands-on experience designing, programming, integrating and commissioning industrial controls for power generation, industrial plants, utilities, or mission-critical infrastructure.

 - Strong hands-on experience with PLC, DCS, SCADA, historian, industrial-networking, and control-system integration.

 - Experience with plant power control, generator controls, synchronization, load sharing, islanding and load-shedding schemes.

 - Experience integrating controls with power generation equipment, protective relays, SCADA/EPMS and other plant systems.

 - Experience developing functional specifications, sequences, I/O, alarms, graphics, and factory or site test procedures.

 - Ability to troubleshoot across software, instrumentation, electrical, mechanical, communications, and operating-process boundaries.

 - Understanding of industrial cybersecurity, redundancy, failover, and change-control practices.

 - Bachelor's degree in controls, electrical, mechanical, chemical engineering, computer engineering, or a related field.

Preferred Skills

 - Experience with major turbine or reciprocating-engine control platforms and microgrid controllers.

 - Experience with data center power systems and rapidly changing AI or GPU loads.

 - Experience integrating gas generation with BESS, MV UPS and grid-forming or grid-following inverters.

 - Experience with EMT studies and model validation for weak-grid or islanded power systems.

 - Experience developing automated simulation tests and regression test libraries.

 - Experience with network redundancy, industrial protocols, OT cybersecurity and remote support for critical facilities.

 - Experience transitioning from temporary generation to permanent power systems.

 - Experience with IEC 61850 (MMS, GOOSE, SV), Modbus, OPC UA, DNP3, EtherNet/IP, or comparable industrial protocols.

 - Professional Engineer license, functional-safety training, or industrial-cybersecurity certification.



About OpenAI

location: Remote - CA; Remote - Chicago; Remote - Seattle; Remote - TX
description:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role:
Samsara's Customer Success team is on the front lines of business value delivery by helping customers adopt our platform, realize measurable business value, and renew and expand with confidence. Today, billing errors, concession requests, and cancellation or return exceptions land with CSMs, CS managers, and several partner teams, each holding part of the picture. No one owns the whole timeline. We are creating a dedicated Contract and Billing Resolution team to close that gap for Mid-Market and Commercial accounts.
As the Manager, Contract and Billing, you will lead this new team of 3 to 4 Contract and Billing Resolution Specialists. You will inherit work that CSMs and their managers have handled as best they can, and turn it into a function that is repeatable, measurable, and scalable: the playbook, the intake and routing, the system of record, the root-cause reporting, and the hiring and coaching of the people who do the work.
This role sits between the sales process and the finance process. A bill can look wrong because of something that happened upstream in a quote, an order form, a contract, or a segment change in Salesforce, or downstream in billing and invoicing. You and your team will figure out where it broke, regardless of which team caused it, and work across both sides to fix it. You will partner closely with Customer Success Managers, Sales, Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal, and report the repeat failures to the teams that own the underlying systems and processes.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every billing case your team resolves keeps the organizations that move goods, transport students, and restore power focused on their operations rather than on a billing dispute.
You want to build something from the ground up: This team and function are new. You will hire the team, write the playbook, and set up the systems and metrics that define how Samsara resolves billing and contract cases.
You thrive when solving problems: You figure things out, even without a clean playbook or precedent. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you find the fix that works for the customer and for Samsara, and you teach your team to do the same.
You are an investigator: You enjoy rebuilding a timeline from incomplete or conflicting records across sales and finance systems, and you stay curious until the numbers tie out.
You are a people leader: You enjoy hiring, coaching, and developing a team, and you set a high bar for quality, ownership, and follow-through.
You are a natural relationship builder: Whether with our customers or cross-functional teams at Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team, and you can maintain clear boundaries while staying warm.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together, and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals.
In this role, you will:
Build and lead a new team of 3 to 4 Contract and Billing Resolution Specialists: hire, onboard, coach, and develop them, and set clear expectations for case quality, ownership, and customer communication.
Stand up the function from scratch: take the billing, concession, and cancellation work that CSMs handle today, define what the team owns and what it does not, and turn it into a documented playbook that is repeatable and scalable.
Design and launch the system of record for billing and contract cases, working with CS Ops and Systems partners to set up intake, routing, case tracking, and customer communication in tools such as Zendesk, Salesforce, or Jira.
Own the front door: make sure every billing, concession, and cancellation request is logged in one place, including those that arrive through Slack, email, or Gainsight, and coach CSMs and AEs on what a complete request looks like.
Act as the escalation point for the most complex, sensitive, or high-dollar cases, including accounts that are delinquent or facing suspension, and step in directly with customers and internal leaders when needed.
Define the handoffs, ownership, and service levels with Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal so cases stop bouncing between teams.
Set the standards for how the team separates a correction of a Samsara error from a concession, a return, a reprocess, and a contract amendment, and how concession and cancellation exceptions are sized, documented, and routed through the approval matrix.
Build the metrics and reporting for the function, including volume, days to resolution, repeat errors, concession dollars, and renewal risk tied to billing issues, and use them to manage the team and show impact.
Fix repeat causes: own the root-cause tagging on every case, separate one-offs from systemic failures, and deliver a monthly read-out to the teams that own the systems and processes involved, such as segment-move bugs, term rounding, and AE handoff gaps.
Partner with Support, Finance, Sales Ops, and Product on billing improvement work, including earlier detection of billing problems that threaten renewals.
Use AI to improve how the team works, from structuring case timelines to drafting summaries, while keeping approvals, amounts, and root-cause conclusions with people.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's operating principles, including Keep a High Bar, Be Intellectually Honest, and Solve Problems Together, as we scale.
Minimum requirements for the role:
7+ years of experience in sales operations, deal desk, contracts, billing operations, order to cash, revenue operations, or a similar finance and operations role.
2+ years of experience managing people, ideally in a sales operations or finance capacity.
Experience building a team or function from scratch, or leading a major reorganization of an existing team, including writing the playbook and processes that made the work repeatable.
Deep working knowledge of either the quote-to-contract side (quotes, order forms, amendments, terms, and the sales systems that pass contract data downstream) or the billing side (invoicing, credits, rebills, and collections), and the curiosity to learn the other.
Experience setting up or significantly improving a case management, ticketing, or request-routing system, such as Zendesk, Jira, or Salesforce cases, that worked for both customers and internal teams.
Strong investigative skills: you can rebuild a timeline from incomplete or conflicting information across CRM, billing, and contract systems, and teach others to do the same.
Sound financial judgment about credits, concessions, reprocessing, and refunds, and a clear way of explaining your recommendation.
A record of driving results across teams without authority over them, including Sales, Finance, and Operations partners with competing priorities.
Customer-facing communication that stays honest and composed in hard conversations, and written summaries a leader can read once and decide on.
This is a demanding position with high internal visibility that requires strong priority management, high emotional intelligence, and comfort with ambiguity and incomplete precedent.
An ideal candidate also has:

title: Account Executive, SMB (Hunter)
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
The SMB team is a high-velocity sales team focused on acquiring new, under-penetrated SMB customers. As an Account Executive on the SMB Hunter sales team, you’ll be responsible for sourcing and closing net new business, executing outbound sales strategies, and running end-to-end sales cycles to bring new customers onto Stripe. You’ll play a critical role in expanding Stripe’s reach by identifying high-potential prospects and converting them into long-term users of our platform.
What you’ll do
As a Account Executive, SMB Hunter you will play an instrumental role in fueling Stripe’s growth by acquiring net new SMB customers. In this role, you will also help build out a new team and go-to-market (GTM) motion at Stripe.
Responsibilities
Identify high-potential prospective users and use effective prospecting strategies to generate leads that drive net-new revenue growth in your territory
Develop and implement scaled sales strategies for acquiring new customers and driving adoption of Stripe’s products across new accounts
Identify and understand users’ pain points to propose Stripe solutions and own the full sales cycle, from business case development to close
Work cross-functionally to solve user pain points and improve our product to better serve new customer needs
Who you are
We’re looking for a high performing, well-rounded seller who can manage high velocity deal cycles, enjoys building and has demonstrated success dealing with ambiguity and operating in a high-growth environment. If you're hungry, persistent and willing to roll up your sleeves to build the plane while we’re flying it, we want to hear from you!
Minimum requirements
2+ years of sales or prospecting experience, preferably at a technology company, with a track record of top performance
Ability to understand complex technical ecosystems and build great relationships with technical customers
Analytical ability to manage complex sales cycles
Experience managing projects with input from cross-functional teams
A knack for working well with a wide range of stakeholders, both internally and externally
Ability and motivation to operate in a highly ambiguous and fast-paced environment
Superior verbal and written communication skills
Proven ability to meet or exceed sales targets
